quarterly_data.signal: CCO Sam Pearce broke out the XYWAV net patient adds by indication in Q&A: '200 for narcolepsy, 325 for idiopathic hypersomnia. In total, 525 net patient adds.' He called that the best quarter in a year - 'Actually, the highest number of adds that we've had for a year' - and said the brand 'is proving itself to be very durable in the face of multi-source generics,' because the differentiation factors have not changed - still the only low sodium oxybate on the market and the only product approved for IH.
quarterly_data.figure: net patient adds 200 narcolepsy + 325 idiopathic hypersomnia = 525; highest add number in a year

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Phil Johnson quantified how much the XYWAV outlook moved on slower generic uptake: 'before we had expected the product to be flat to up mid-single digits this year, and now we're expecting double-digit growth for the full year.' He said 'To date, uptake of high-sodium generics has been quite limited,' that the first-half impact played out as expected, but 'based on the pace of introduction of the high sodium generics, we're now expecting a much more muted impact in the back half of the year as well.' He added that this strengthens Jazz's position in go-forward payer discussions, and declined to guide 2027 until the fourth quarter 2026 call.
quarterly_data.figure: XYWAV FY2026 expectation moved from flat to up mid-single digits to double-digit growth

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Renee Gala sized the remaining idiopathic hypersomnia runway, saying Jazz is 'still very early in our overall penetration' and that 'We think there's probably 37,000+ patients diagnosed and seeking treatment for IH.' On durability against generics and the coming orexin agonists, CMO Rob Iannone said XYWAV is differentiated on low sodium, that the XYWAV study showed that 'after initiation of high sodium oxybate, you see a change in blood pressure, which is clinically meaningful,' that patients benefiting from XYWAV 'will be pretty sticky,' and that orexins are complementary daytime wake-promoting agents rather than replacements, because only oxybate addresses the disrupted nighttime sleep that is the root cause.
quarterly_data.figure: 37,000+ IH patients diagnosed and seeking treatment

quarterly_data.signal: Asked what drove the Epidiolex upside, CCO Sam Pearce said the 16% growth 'taking us to $292 million for the quarter' was '12% volume growth,' reflecting strong demand in both the pediatric and the adult settings and reinforcing Jazz's position as 'the number one branded anti-seizure medication in refractory epilepsy,' with continued headroom in the long-term care setting. He said there were 'no really significant unusual inventory movements.' CFO Phil Johnson added that one-time pricing adjustments in a couple of ex-U.S. markets had depressed second quarter 2025 revenue, creating favorability on this year's compare, and that FX also helped ex-U.S. revenue in the first half - most pronounced in the first quarter and coming down significantly in the second quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: Epidiolex 12% volume growth inside 16% revenue growth to $292 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Renee Gala put economics on the Epidiolex franchise, describing 'the visibility of long durability into the very late 2030s now with this franchise' and saying 'We paid a little over $7 billion for what is a franchise that is growing nicely, over $1 billion a year, with the opportunity to grow in multiple formulations through clinical data and also internationally.' On intellectual property she said the capsule launch 'does not have any impact on IP. It does not have any impact on our ANDA agreements that extend the durability,' out to the very late 2030s, and that the patent estate 'contains method of use patents that are relevant to all approved indications,' covering both the existing oral solution and the new capsule formulation.
quarterly_data.figure: a little over $7 billion paid for the Epidiolex franchise; growing over $1 billion a year; durability into the very late 2030s

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Sam Pearce laid out the commercial case for the Epidiolex capsule formulation: it 'will enable us to capture naive patients, improve persistency in existing patients, and encourage restarts for patients that maybe started on the oral solid dose on the liquid, and it wasn't the best treatment for them,' aimed particularly at 'those adolescent and adult patients, where the oral liquid solution is a less convenient option for them.' He called it 'a material incremental opportunity that will drive more patients benefiting from Epidiolex,' and said the capsule is designed to unlock additional utilization inside the already approved indications by reaching deeper into segments of the adult patient population. Preparing for the oral solid dose launch is part of the raised SG&A investment.

CCO Sam Pearce said first-line maintenance is now the engine of Zepzelca, which delivered '42% growth this quarter, taking us to $106 million': 'We estimate now that between 30%-40% of our overall U.S. sales are coming from that first-line maintenance segment,' and that share is growing. He cited the NCCN listing 'elevated to Category 1 as a preferred regimen in first-line maintenance in combination with Tecentriq,' and said the second-line business has been declining on competition and because patients started on Zepzelca in the front line are not retreated in second line - erosion that Jazz 'may expect to accelerate' after the label announcement, all of which 'is factored into the guidance that we've provided for this year.'
quarterly_data.figure: 30%-40% of U.S. Zepzelca sales from first-line maintenance; Zepzelca $106 million, +42%

quarterly_data.signal: CMO Rob Iannone said that based on the results of the LAGOON trial and in alignment with FDA, 'in 3Q 2026, we will submit for FDA's review and subsequent action a labeling supplement to remove the second-line indication,' adding that 'The first-line maintenance indication will not be affected.' He said the IMforte trial was designed to preempt progression in an aggressive disease on the hypothesis that Zepzelca would synergize with a PD-L1 inhibitor like atezolizumab, and that data published at ASCO on the impact of tumor-associated macrophages explains the potential synergy with a PD-L1 agent, supporting front line as the best place to use Zepzelca.
quarterly_data.figure: second-line labeling supplement to be submitted in 3Q 2026; first-line maintenance indication unaffected

quarterly_data.signal: CCO Sam Pearce detailed the zanidatamab GEA launch readiness: 'We have more than 90% physician overlap between GEA treating centers,' access already established through 'the permanent J-code already active from the BTC approval,' the data submitted to Oncology Pathways, a newly onboarded team of clinical nurse educators, and the JazzCares patient support program. He said the team was sized specifically with a GEA launch in mind and that readiness combined with the data 'means that we should see really very rapid uptake,' with BTC serving as 'a powerful commercial foundation for our next major growth phase in GEA' given the significant direct overlap between BTC and GEA treating accounts.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 90% physician overlap between GEA treating centers; permanent J-code already active

quarterly_data.signal: CMO Rob Iannone described the zanidatamab plus chemotherapy doublet arm, which 'showed a clinically meaningful survival benefit with a median OS of more than two years and a strong trend towards statistical significance at the time of the first interim OS analysis.' Subgroup data presented at ASCO confirmed that the zanidatamab plus tislelizumab combination 'delivers a consistent survival benefit irrespective of PD-L1 tumor expression.' Jazz submitted The New England Journal of Medicine manuscript for potential inclusion in the NCCN guidelines and said NCCN has 'everything they need to adopt that into the guidelines, potentially even before approval.'
quarterly_data.figure: doublet median OS of more than two years; survival benefit irrespective of PD-L1 tumor expression

quarterly_data.signal: CMO Rob Iannone said zanidatamab 'was recently granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation for adults with previously treated locally advanced, unresectable, or metastatic HER2-positive colorectal cancer,' supported by previously published colorectal data plus emerging data from the ongoing 206 basket study, which continues to enroll second-line colorectal cancer and non-small cell lung cancer patients. Jazz will work with FDA now that it has BTD to identify the path forward to approval in colorectal cancer, and is also contemplating early gastric cancer, 'where there's no approved HER2 therapy,' alongside the ongoing frontline BTC trial and phase II combination trials in breast cancer.
quarterly_data.figure: Breakthrough Therapy Designation in HER2-positive colorectal cancer; 206 basket study ongoing in second-line CRC and NSCLC

quarterly_data.signal: CMO Rob Iannone sized the post-Enhertu breast cancer opportunity at 'roughly 150,000 patients annually,' returning later in the call to clarify that '150,000 really represents the pool of metastatic patients globally' and that the treatable group is the subset who have progressed and remain eligible for treatment. The phase III trial is global, positioned in patients who have been treated with Enhertu - typically third-line plus - and is run 'head-to-head against trastuzumab.' He confirmed Jazz is 'on track to complete enrollment by mid-year 2027,' with results expected 'late 2027 or early 2028' depending on how events accrue.
quarterly_data.figure: roughly 150,000 metastatic patients globally; enrollment complete by mid-year 2027; results late 2027 or early 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Phil Johnson said the non-GAAP adjusted gross margin 'declined slightly year-on-year due to higher sales of Zepzelca and Modeyso, which carry third-party royalties' - the mix effect of the two faster-growing, royalty-bearing oncology products on portfolio profitability.
quarterly_data.figure: non-GAAP adjusted gross margin declined slightly year-on-year on third-party royalties for Zepzelca and Modeyso

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Phil Johnson said the non-GAAP adjusted effective tax rate in the quarter was 'moderately higher than our full-year 2026 guidance due to shifts in the expected geographic mix of income and expenses,' and that shares outstanding for the quarter 'reflect the accounting effect of our higher share price on our convertible notes and employee stock plans.' Updated share count guidance is 69 million-70 million shares, reflecting the increase in the stock price since the last earnings call. During the second quarter Jazz 'paid off our 2026 convertible notes.'
quarterly_data.figure: share count guidance 69 million-70 million shares; 2026 convertible notes paid off during the quarter

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Renee Gala described the business development machine: Jazz remains 'highly engaged on the BD front,' having 'hired a new CBO earlier this year to drive those efforts,' and continues 'to expect to announce one or more deals still in 2026.' The screen is significant unmet need where Jazz's expertise, global footprint or existing operations can have a meaningful impact, plus 'an efficiency of commercial call point' where its patient support services are relevant and valued; focus areas are rare epilepsy, rare sleep and rare oncology, and other areas of rare disease. On stage, Jazz is working from preclinical deals like AbCellera through to 'later pipeline deals as well as commercial and near commercial transactions,' citing a track record of Epidiolex from GW, the near-commercial 'Modeyso Chimerix transaction' and zanidatamab, which also came into the business via business development.
